pr_body:
This adds the ability to perform date math: allow date types be updated with a time span (a duration or a period).

Ex. : `row n = now() | eval then = n - 1 year + 2 minutes`

Closes #98402.
pr_title: ESQL: Add ability to perform date math
pr_comment: Hi @bpintea, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

> The main comment I have is around the use of timezones.
> If that is not the case, this should be clarified.

I've added a comment.

> Lastly some docs help - I would reuse the structure and content from SQL since its fairly similar.

Will follow with a subsequent PR.

> unit tests tests for period + datetime and duration + datetime

added.

> unit tests for period - datetime and duration - datetime

Good point, thanks. Increased the Sub type resolution checks to prevent this.

> unit or csv tests for weird edge cases, like date math for leap years, adding days or hours past the end of a month, etc. Although this may be less important since we know that we can trust the date math functions from the ql package.

Indeed, left this out.

review_comment:
nit: I think it'd be easier for readability to separate out the unrepresentable case into a separate helper function, e.g. `processTimeSpanLiteral` or so.

The test cases for numerics and for durations/periods seem to be pretty distinct, and it's a bit confusing when reading the code of the `process` method, that we do vastly different things only if we encounter an unrepresentable type (while actually meaning a time span, which happens to be unrepresentable). The unrepresentable case here is irrelevant for all numeric test cases and vice versa, so it might be clearer to just separate it out.

This helper function would still need to be invoked from `process()`, since I'd like to avoid having the test cases "decide" how to "process" the negation. This being a test, I've just added a small comment on the else branch.
nit: similarly here, wouldn't we want to use `expectedValue` here?
nit: variable naming is somewhat unclear IMO, maybe renaming to e.g. `datetimesEvaluator` would be clearer?
I wanted to stay consistent with the name of the other type evaluators (both fields - like `ints` and evaluator class name - like `SubDatetimesEvaluator`).
praise: good call testing the `Neg` edge cases :)
nit: don't we want to use `expectedValue` here and in line 100?

We would want that, but the `TestCaseSupplier`s are built statically and the `expectedValue()` is inherited/overridden; otherwise we could have used the `resultMatcher()` method directly (which would have been even nicer).
